title: Evaluation Of Change in Corneal Biomechanics Following Non-Penetrating Deep Sclerectomy compared to Trabeculectomy or Paul-Implant in Glaucoma Patients: Insights From Ocular Response Analyzer (ORA) Measurements
summary:
The scientific project "Pre- and postoperative investigation of the biomechanics of the eye in glaucoma surgeries and the study of predispositions for the development of glaucoma" is a monocentric study that examines changes in the biomechanics of the eye in patients before and after glaucoma surgeries. The purpose of this study is to provide an overview of how the biomechanics of the eye change after different types of glaucoma surgeries, including globe-opening procedures, non-globe-opening procedures, and surgeries involving drainage implants.

The study will measure various clinical parameters, such as intraocular pressure, the number of pressure-lowering eye drops required, retinal nerve fiber layer thickness as measured by OCT, corneal hysteresis (a measure of the biomechanical properties of the cornea), and visual field defects. The goal is to determine how these parameters and the biomechanics of the eye are affected by different glaucoma surgeries.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with primary open-angle glaucoma, pseudoexfoliation glaucoma, pigment dispersion glaucoma and (with Paul tube implants) secondary glaucoma
Exclusion criteria:
Non-consenting adults (≥ 18 years), children and adolescents (< 18 years), others (e.g. persons in closed institutions / in prison)
